preface.p: English is not an official language of the Swiss Confederation. This translation is provided for information purposes only and has no legal force.

p.docTitle:
Ordinance
on the Incentive Tax on Volatile Organic Compounds

preamble.p:
based on Articles 35a and 35c of the Environmental Protection Act of 7 October 1983
SR 814.01 (EPA),

content.p: For the purpose of this Ordinance, volatile organic compounds (VOCs) are organic compounds with a vapour pressure of at least 0.1 mbar at 20 °C or a boiling point of maximum 240 °C at 1013.25 mbar.

blockList.listIntroduction: The following are liable for tax:

item.p: VOCs on the positive list of substances (Annex 1);
VOCs in accordance with letter a that are contained in imported mixtures and products mentioned in the positive list of products (Annex 2).

content.p: Customs legislation applies by analogy to the levying and refund of the tax, and to the procedure where imports and exports are concerned.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the O of 27 June 2012, in force since 1 Jan. 2013 (AS 2012 3785).

content.p: The Directorate General of Customs shall implement this Ordinance unless the Federal Office for the Environment (FOEN) is responsible. In doing so, it shall take account of the views of the FOEN.

blockList.listIntroduction: The FOEN:

item.p: implements the provisions on the distribution of the tax revenue (Art. 23–23b);

item.num:
b.
Repealed by No I of the O of 23 Feb. 2022, with effect from 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2022 160).

item.p: evaluates the effect on air quality of the tax and the exemption from tax in cases of measures taken to reduce emissions and publishes the results regularly.

content.p:
The Federal Office for Customs and Border Security (FOCBS) shall provide the FOEN with the required documents.
Amended by No I of the O of 23 Feb. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2022 160).

blockList.listIntroduction: The cantons shall support the federal implementing authorities, unless the Confederation is liable to the tax. In particular, they shall review:

item.p: the verification of the proof in accordance with Article 9h;
the verification of the VOC balance sheets in accordance with Article 10;

the confirmation of the reduction of diffuse emissions in accordance with Article 9k.
Amended by No I of the O of 23 Feb. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2022 160).

content.p:
The costs incurred by the federal implementing authorities shall be compensated for annually at 4.9 per cent of the revenue (gross revenue less refunds). The amount of the compensation for implementation shall be verified and modified if required.
Amended by No I of the O of 23 Feb. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2022 160).

In consultation with the Federal Department of Finance, the Federal Department of Environment, Transport, Energy and Communications (DETEC) shall issue regulations on compensatory payments to the cantons for their support in implementing this Ordinance.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the O of 11 May 2011, in force since 1 Jan. 2012 (AS 2011 1951).

article.heading: Commission of experts for the incentive tax on VOCs

content.p:
The Federal Council shall establish a commission of experts, on which the Confederation, the cantons and other interested parties are represented, and shall appoint a representative of the FOEN
Expression in accordance with No I of the O of 27 June 2012, in force since 1 Jan. 2013 (AS 2012 3785). This amendment has been made throughout the text. as president. The commission of experts shall consist of a maximum of twelve members.

The commission of experts shall advise the Confederation and the cantons on matters relating to the incentive tax on VOCs, in particular on the amendment of the Annexes and on the implementation of the exemption from tax in cases of measures taken to reduce emissions.
Amended by No I of the O of 27 June 2012, in force since 1 Jan. 2013 (AS 2012 3785).

The implementing authorities may, without prior notice, carry out audits, in particular of persons who are required to pay the tax, and of persons required to prepare a VOC balance sheet or who submit a request for a refund
Term in accordance with No I of the O of 23 Feb. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2022 160). This change has been made throughout the text..
All information and documents necessary for the implementation of this Ordinance must be submitted to the implementing authorities on request.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the O of 2 April 2008, in force since 1 Jan. 2009 (AS 2008 1765).

content.p: The tax rate amounts to 3 Swiss francs per kilogram of VOCs.

section.heading: Exemption from Tax and VOC Balance Sheet

article.heading: Exemption from tax in cases of negligible quantities

blockList.listIntroduction: VOCs in the following mixtures and products are exempt from tax:

item.p: mixtures and products in which the VOC content does not exceed 3 per cent (% by weight);

item.num:
b.
Amended by No I of the O of 23 Feb. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2022 160).
item.p: mixtures and products that are not on the positive list of products.

content.p:
…
Repealed by No I of the O of 23 Feb. 2022, with effect from 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2022 160).

If mixtures and products in accordance with paragraph 1 letters a and b are manufactured in Switzerland, the VOCs contained therein are exempted from tax at the request
Term in accordance with No I of the O of 23 Feb. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2022 160). This change has been made throughout the text. of the manufacturer.

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the O of 27 June 2012, in force since 1 Jan. 2013 (AS 2012 3785).

article.heading: Exemption from tax in cases of measures taken to reduce emissions

blockList.listIntroduction:
VOCs that are used in stationary installations in terms of Article 2 paragraph 1 and Annex 1 Number 32 of the Ordinance on Air Pollution Control of 16 December 1985
SR 814.318.142.1 (OAPC) are exempt from the tax if:

item.p: the measures taken have resulted in the annual quantity of VOC emissions from these installations being reduced by at least 50 per cent of the VOC emissions quantity allowed for the same rate of production while complying with the preventive emission limits set by Articles 3 and 4 of the OAPC;
the air purification plant (APP) used therefor is in a good technical condition and is operational for 95 per cent of the operating time; and
the VOC emissions of the stationary installation that are not processed by the APP (diffuse VOC emissions) are reduced in accordance with Annex 3.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 27 June 2012, in force since 1 Jan. 2013 (AS 2012 3785).

blockList.listIntroduction: Two or more stationary installations may on application be combined as an installation group if:

item.p: they are operated by the same person; and

each installation meets the requirements of the OAPC.
Amended by No I of the O of 13 Feb. 2013, in force since 1 March 2013 (AS 2013 573).

content.p: An installation group is treated in the same way as a single stationary installation with regard to meeting the exemption requirements set out in Article 9.

blockList.listIntroduction: The composition of an installation group may not be changed in the following cases. Exempted therefrom are:

item.p: the exclusion of decommissioned stationary installations;
the subsequent inclusion of stationary installations that already meet the requirements set out in Annex 3;

the amendment of Annex 3; only from the date on which the amendment comes into force.
Amended by No I of the O of 23 Feb. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2022 160).

content.p:
…
Repealed by No I of the O of 23 Feb. 2022, with effect from 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2022 160).

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 27 June 2012, in force since 1 Jan. 2013 (AS 2012 3785).

article.heading: Exceptional events and replacement of the APP

blockList.listIntroduction: If the operational targets for the APP required under Article 9 paragraph 1 letter b are not achieved over a financial year due to an exceptional event, the VOCs emitted outside the downtime of the APP are exempt from the tax provided:

item.p: the exemption requirements set out in Article 9 are met outside the downtime;
the cantonal authority was informed immediately of the exceptional event; and
the exceptional event was not caused by the inadequate maintenance or incorrect operation of the APP.

blockList.listIntroduction: If the operational targets for the APP required under Article 9 paragraph 1 letter b are not achieved over a financial year due to the replacement of the APP, the VOCs emitted outside the downtime of the APP are exempt from the tax provided:

item.p: the exemption requirements set out in Article 9 are met outside the period during which the APP was being replaced;
the cantonal authority is informed in advance of the planned downtime of the APP; and
the replacement work is carried out during the company holidays or at times of low production.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 27 June 2012 (AS 2012 3785). Amended by No I of the O of 23 Feb. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2022 160).

article.heading: Modifications in line with the state of the art

content.p: DETEC shall modify Annex 3 in line with technical developments after consulting the industries and cantons concerned.

The VOC emissions from stationary installations that are no longer reduced in accordance with the requirements of Annex 3 because of modifications pursuant to paragraph 1 remain exempt from the tax provided the installation meets the requirements of Annex 3 once again within three years of the date on which the modification comes into force.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 27 June 2012 (AS 2012 3785). Repealed by No I of the O of 23 Feb. 2022, with effect from 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2022 160).
Inserted by No I of the O of 27 June 2012, in force since 1 Jan. 2013 (AS 2012 3785).

article.heading:
Modifications of the stationary installation
Amended by No I of the O of 23 Feb. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2022 160).

content.p: Modifications of the stationary installation that affect the diffuse VOC emissions must be reported to the cantonal authority immediately.

…
Repealed by No I of the O of 23 Feb. 2022, with effect from 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2022 160).

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 27 June 2012, in force since 1 Jan. 2013 (AS 2012 3785).

article.heading:
Proof required for the tax exemption
Amended by No I of the O of 23 Feb. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2022 160).

content.p:
Any person who claims a tax exemption under Article 35a paragraph 4 EPA must prove each year that the exemption requirements set out in Article 9 have been met.
Amended by No I of the O of 23 Feb. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2022 160).
The proof must be submitted at the same time as the VOC balance sheet.
If the proof cannot be provided, the tax exemption ceases to apply to the VOCs used in the stationary installation during the relevant financial year.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 25 Oct. 2017 (AS 2017 5953). Repealed by No I of the O of 23 Feb. 2022, with effect from 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2022 160).
Inserted by No I of the O of 25 Oct. 2017 (AS 2017 5953). Amended by No I of the O of 23 Feb. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2022 160).

content.p: Stationary installations become exempt from the tax from the date that they meet the requirements for an exemption under Article 9.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 23 Feb. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2022 160).

article.heading: Confirmation of the reduction in diffuse emissions

content.p: In the case of stationary installations, the cantons shall confirm compliance with the requirements of Annex 3 if so requested by the operator.
They shall review the confirmations at least every five years and shall conduct inspections in order to do so.

Any person who claims an exemption from the tax in accordance with Article 35a paragraph 3 letter c or paragraph 4 of the EPA or an authorisation to obtain VOCs provisionally exempted from the tax (Art. 21) shall keep VOC accounts and prepare a VOC balance sheet.
Amended by No I of the O of 14 Dec. 1998, in force since 1 Jan. 1999 (AS 1999 604).

blockList.listIntroduction: A VOC balance sheet shall contain:

item.p: quantities contained in mixtures and products;
quantities eliminated in the enterprise or through an external enterprise, or quantities transformed;

content.p:
The implementing authorities may request further information.
Amended by No I of the O of 23 Feb. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2022 160).
The VOC balance sheet must be prepared on an official form. The Directorate General of Customs may accept other manners of presentation.
If the cost of preparing VOC balance sheets is disproportionately high, the Directorate General of Customs may grant exceptions to paragraphs 1 and 2.
Persons who produce VOCs must report to the Directorate General of Customs, which shall maintain a register.

blockList.listIntroduction: A tax demand is made:

item.p: for VOCs produced within Switzerland, at the moment when they leave the manufacturer, or are used by the manufacturer;
for VOCs subject to subsequent payment of the tax under Article 22 paragraph 2, at the moment when the beneficiary uses the VOCs, or passes them on to a third party.

content.p:
Manufacturers who place VOCs on the market or use them themselves, as well as persons who supply VOCs wholesale and possess an authorisation to obtain VOCs provisionally exempted from the tax (Art. 21 para. 2) must submit a tax declaration to the Directorate General of Customs by the 25th day of the month following the origin of the tax demand.
Amended by No I of the O of 27 June 2012, in force since 1 Jan. 2013 (AS 2012 3785).

Persons who are required to pay the tax subsequently in accordance with Article 22 paragraph 2 must submit a tax declaration to the cantonal authorities within six months of the end of their financial year.

The declaration shall contain details of the type and quantity of the VOCs placed on the market or used. It shall be made on an official form. The Directorate General of Customs may accept other manners of presentation.
The declaration serves as a basis for assessing the tax. The relevant authorities reserve the right of review.

Any person who fails to complete the tax declaration in full or to submit it on time shall pay interest on the tax due.
Inserted by No I of the O of 14 Dec. 1998, in force since 1 Jan. 1999 (AS 1999 604)
The tax is calculated on the basis of the quantity of VOCs at the time the tax demand is made.
The Directorate General of Customs shall assess the amount of tax in a ruling.
The period allowed for payment shall be 30 days.
Interest shall be payable in the case of late payment.

If the Directorate General of Customs should inadvertently fail to assess a tax which is due, or if the assessment is too low or any refund is too high, it may demand the amount due within one year of the notification of the ruling.
The tax demand shall prescribe ten years after the end of the calendar year in which it originated.

blockList.listIntroduction: The prescriptive period shall be interrupted:

item.p: if the tax payer acknowledges the tax demand;
by each official act by which the tax demand is made to the tax payer.

content.p: The prescriptive period starts again following each interruption.
The tax demand prescribes in every case fifteen years after the end of the calendar year in which it originated.

Tax is refunded only if the entitled persons prove that they have used the VOCs in such a way that these are exempt from the tax.
Amended by No I of the O of 2 April 2008, in force since 1 Jan. 2009 (AS 2008 1765).
Entitled persons must retain all documents necessary for the justification of a refund for five years after submitting a request for a refund.
If the requested refund is less than 3000 Swiss francs, it shall not be paid. The foregoing does not apply to refunds of at least 300 Swiss francs for the export of VOCs.

Two or more entitled persons may form a group and submit a joint request for a refund. The payment of the refund shall be made to the representative designated by the group.
Inserted by No I of the O of 2 April 2008, in force since 1 Jan. 2009 (AS 2008 1765).

Entitled persons must prove that the tax has been paid.
Amended by No I of the O of 2 April 2008, in force since 1 Jan. 2009 (AS 2008 1765).
Requests for refund may be made only after the end of the financial year unless they concern an export.

article.heading: Forfeiture of the right to a refund

content.p:
The right to a refund, unless it concerns an export, must be claimed within six months of the end of the financial year. The FOCBS may on request extend this deadline by 30 days in justified cases.
Amended by No I of the O of 23 Feb. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2022 160).
The right to a refund expires in all cases two years after the grounds for a refund originated.

blockList.listIntroduction: The request for a refund must be made on an official form and be submitted to:

item.p: the Directorate General of Customs, in the case of exported VOCs.

blockList.listIntroduction: In the case of exported VOCs, the request must contain:

item.p: the quantity of VOCs exported over a maximum period of twelve months, as declared on the export documents;
reports on manufacture, samples contained in their original packaging, or other documentation required to assess the quantity of VOCs exported;
any further information required for the calculation of the request for a refunded by the Directorate General of Customs.

section.heading:
Obtaining VOCs provisionally exempt from Tax (Procedure for Formal Commitment)
Amended by No I of the O of 14 Dec. 1998, in force since 1 Jan. 1999 (AS 1999 604)

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the O of 14 Dec. 1998, in force since 1 Jan. 1999 (AS 1999 604)

blockList.listIntroduction:
The FOCBS may authorise persons to acquire VOCs provisionally exempt from tax provided that they undertake:
Amended by No I of the O of 23 Feb. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2022 160).

item.p: to use or handle at least 25t of VOCs per annum in such a way that they are not released to the environment;
to export at least 25t of VOCs per annum;

item.num:
c.
Inserted by No I of the O of 23 Feb. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2022 160).
item.p: to process at least 25t of VOCs per annum into mixtures or products in which content does not exceed 3 per cent (% by weight); or

item.num:
d.
Inserted by No I of the O of 23 Feb. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2022 160).
item.p:
to process at least 25t of VOCs per annum into mixtures or products that are not listed on the positive list of products.
Amended by No I of the O of 26 June 2002, in force since 1 Dec. 2002 (AS 2002 3117).

content.p:
…
Inserted by No I of the O of 4 Dec. 2000 (AS 2000 3049). Repealed by No I of the O of 27 June 2012, with effect from 1 Jan. 2013 (AS 2012 3785).

blockList.listIntroduction: It may also grant this authorisation to persons who use a substance listed in Annex 1 of this Ordinance if they prove that:

item.p: this substance amounts to at least 55 per cent of their entire consumption of VOCs;
they use at least 1 tonne of this substance each year; and

due to chemical transformation caused by the process for using the substance, on average no more than 2 per cent of the substance is released to the environment.
Inserted by No I of the O of 27 June 2012, in force since 1 Jan. 2013 (AS 2012 3785).

content.p:
Authorisation may also be granted to persons who deal wholesale in VOCs and prove average stocks of at least 10t of VOCs or an annual minimum turnover of 25 t of VOCs.
Amended by No I of the O of 23 Feb. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2022 160).
The formal commitment or the proof must be submitted to the Directorate General of Customs.

The Directorate General of Customs shall maintain a public register of persons who have been authorised to acquire provisionally exempted VOCs.
Inserted by No I of the O of 27 June 2012, in force since 1 Jan. 2013 (AS 2012 3785).
Holders of an authorisation under Article 21 must submit the VOC balance sheet to the cantonal authorities no later than six months after the end of the financial year.
For VOCs used in such a way that they are not exempt from tax, payments of the tax must be made subsequently.

.…
Repealed by No I of the O of 2 April 2008, in force since 1 June 2008 (AS 2008 1765).

Documents relating to the procedure for obtaining VOC provisionally exempt from tax must be retained for five years after submission of the VOC balance sheet.
Amended by No I of the O of 14 Dec. 1998, in force since 1 Jan. 1999 (AS 1999 604).

authorialNote.p: Inserted by Annex 4 No 43 of the Customs Ordinance of 1 Nov. 2006, in force since 1 May 2007 (AS 2007 1469).

content.p:
Any person required to make a customs declaration who applies for a new customs assessment in accordance with Article 34 paragraph 3 of the Customs Act of 18 March 2005
SR 631.0 must prove that an authorisation to obtain VOCs provisionally exempt from tax existed at the time of the original customs declaration.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 2 April 2008, in force since 1 June 2008 (AS 2008 1765).

article.heading: Errors in the submission of VOC balance sheet

content.p:
…
Repealed by No I of the O of 23 Feb. 2022, with effect from 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2022 160).

If the VOC balance sheet is incomplete or has not been submitted on time, the FOCBS shall allow a grace period within which to submit a proper balance sheet.
Amended by No I of the O of 23 Feb. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2022 160).

Interest shall be charged on the taxes due in accordance with Art. 22 paragraph 2 on the basis of the balance sheet submitted during the grace period. The charging of interest begins on expiry of the submission deadline in accordance with Art. 22 paragraph 1.

If the resubmission deadline in accordance with paragraph 2 expires without resubmission being made, the Directorate General of Customs shall assess the tax due in accordance with due discretion and taking account of outgoings taxed in previous years.

authorialNote.p: Inserted by No I of the O of 23 Feb. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2022 160).

blockList.listIntroduction: The FOCBS shall suspend authorisation for the procedure for formal commitment, if:

item.p: obligations to cooperate are breached, in particular if the VOC balance sheet is not submitted by the extended deadline; or
the subsequent payment of the tax for the provisionally exempted VOCs appears to be jeopardised.

blockList.listIntroduction: Payment shall in particular appear to be jeopardised if:

item.p: a credit check indicates that the solvency of the holder of the authorisation is questionable;
the holder of the authorisation has defaulted in making payment; or

the holder of the authorisation is not domiciled in Switzerland or is arranging to give up their domicile or place of business or permanent establishment in Switzerland or to be deleted from the Swiss Commercial Register.

section.heading: Distribution of Revenue from the Tax

authorialNote.p: Amended by No I of the O of 11 May 2011, in force since 1 Jan. 2012, with the exception of para. 7 first sentence, in force since 1 Jan. 2011 (AS 2011 1951).

content.p:
The insurers shall, on behalf and under the supervision of the Federal Office, distribute the revenue from the tax under deduction of the implementation costs to the population as instructed.
Amended by No I of the O of 23 Feb. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2022 160).
The distribution shall be carried out in the next year but one (the year of distribution) based on the annual revenue from the tax obtained in the year of collection.
The annual revenue from the tax corresponds to the revenue collected by 31 December including interest.

blockList.listIntroduction: The insurers are as follows:

item.p:
insurers providing mandatory health insurance in accordance with the Federal Act of 18 March 1994
SR 832.10 on Health Insurance (HIA);

the military insurance fund in accordance with the Federal Act of 19 June 1992
SR 833.1 on Military Insurance (MIA).

blockList.listIntroduction: The insurers shall distribute the annual revenue in equal parts to all those who, in the year of distribution:

item.p: are required to insure themselves in terms of the HIA or of Article 2 paragraph 1 or 2 MIA; and
are domiciled or habitually resident in Switzerland.

content.p:
Persons who are insured for only part of the distribution year shall be entitled to a deduction pro rata temporis.
Amended by Art. 137 of the CO2 Ordinance of 30 Nov. 2012, in force since 1 Jan. 2013 (AS 2012 7005).

The insurers shall offset the amounts against the premiums due in the distribution year.
Amended by Art. 137 of the CO2 Ordinance of 30 Nov. 2012, in force since 1 Jan. 2013 (AS 2012 7005).

authorialNote.p: Inserted by Art. 137 of the CO2 Ordinance of 30 Nov. 2012, in force since 1 Jan. 2013 (AS 2012 7005).

content.p: The annual revenue shall be disbursed to the insurers proportionately by 30 June of each distribution year.
The share paid to each insurer is calculated on the basis of the number of persons that it has insured who meet the requirements of Article 23 paragraph 5 on 1 January of the distribution year.
The difference between the share disbursed and the sum of the amounts actually distributed will in each case be settled in the following year.

authorialNote.p: Originally Art. 23a. Inserted by No I of the O of 11 May 2011, in force since 1 Jan. 2012 (AS 2011 1951).

blockList.listIntroduction: Each insurer shall report the following to the Federal Office of Public Health by 20 March of the distribution year:

item.p: the number of persons that it insures that meet the requirements of Article 23 paragraph 5 as of 1 January of the distribution year;
the sum actually distributed in the previous year.

content.p:
The insurers shall inform the insured persons of the amount to be distributed when notifying them of the new premium for the distribution year. In addition, they must provide the insured persons with a factsheet prepared by the FOEN on the redistribution procedure.
Amended by No III 2 of the O of 4 May 2022, in force since 1 June 2022 (AS 2022 311).

authorialNote.p: Originally Art. 23b. Inserted by No I of the O of 11 May 2011 (AS 2011 1951). Amended by Art. 137 of the CO2 Ordinance of 30 Nov. 2012, in force since 1 Jan. 2013 (AS 2012 7005).

item.p:
Compensation for the insurers is governed by Article 123 of the CO2 Ordinance of 30 November 2012
SR 641.711.

content.p: Manufacturers of VOCs must report to the Directorate General of Customs within three months of this Ordinance coming into force.

article.heading: Commencement and first levy of incentive tax

content.p: This Ordinance comes into force on 1 January 1998.

The incentive tax shall be levied for the first time on 1 January 2000.
Amended by No I of the O of 14 Dec. 1998, in force since 1 Jan. 1999 (AS 1999 604).

transitional.heading:
Transitional Provision to the Amendment of 27 June 2012
AS 2012 3785

content.p: Applications for the approval of a measures plan with a view to obtaining a tax exemption for 2013 must be submitted by 30 April 2013 at the latest.

level.heading: Positive List of Products (Volatile Organic Compounds (VOCs) subject to the Tax)

td.p: Undenatured ethyl alcohol of an alcoholic content of 80 % vol or higher; ethyl alcohol or other spirits, denatured of any strength; not for consumption

item.p: – undenatured ethyl alcohol of an alcoholic strength of 80 % vol or higher
– ethyl alcohol and spirits, denatured, of any strength

td.p: Undenatured ethyl alcohol of an alcoholic strength of less than 80 % vol; spirits, liqueurs and other spirit beverages; not for consumption

item.p: – – undenatured ethyl alcohol of an alcoholic strength by volume of less than 80 % vol.

td.p: Vinegar and substitutes for vinegar obtained from acetic acid, not for consumption

Petroleum oils and oils obtained from bituminous minerals, other than crude; preparations not elsewhere specified or included, containing by weight 70% or more of petroleum oils or of oils obtained from bituminous minerals, these oils being the basic constituents of the preparations, other than those that contain biodiesel and other than waste oils:

item.p: – – mixed mineral oil distillates of which at least 20 % vol distils at under 300°C

td.p: Petroleum oils and oils obtained from bituminous minerals, other than crude; preparations not elsewhere specified or included, containing by weight 70% or more of petroleum oils or of oils obtained from bituminous minerals, these oils being the basic constituents of the preparations and containing biodiesel, other than waste oils:
Petroleum gases and other gaseous hydrocarbons:
Bituminous mixtures based on natural asphalt, on natural bitumen, on petroleum bitumen, on mineral tar or on mineral tar pitch (e.g. asphalt mix, cutback bitumen)

Annex 3
Inserted by No II para. 3 of the O of 27 June 2012 (AS 2012 3785). Revised by No II of the DETEC Ordinance of 28 Nov. 2016 (AS 2016 4923) and No II of the O of 23 Feb. 2022, in force since 1 Jan. 2023 (AS 2022 160).

level.heading: Requirements for the operation of stationary installations

content.p: All VOC relevant processes must be optimised with a view to reducing diffuse VOC emissions.
1 Processes must be conducted in closed systems, provided this is technically and operationally possible and economically acceptable.
2 The exhaust air from closed systems must be processed by the APP.

3 In the case of processes in non-closed systems, the exhaust air must be processed by the APP via suction hoods or shape-adapted source extractors with appropriate suction capacity either directly or following concentration.
4 Room exhaust air must be processed by the APP directly or following concentration.
5 The exhaust air under paragraphs 2–4 must be processed by the APP after production has been completed (APP stopping time).
6 Paragraphs 3–5 do not apply if it is established that the exhaust air due to its negligible VOC concentration is unlikely to be processed by the APP.

blockList.listIntroduction: 7 There must be an up-to-date maintenance plan for the exhaust air system, which in particular sets out how it is guaranteed that:

item.p: the exhaust air system is airtight;
components that are essential to the system are quickly replaced.

blockList.listIntroduction: 8 The ventilation in working spaces with mechanically generated incoming air must be operated, provided this is technically and operationally possible and economically feasible, so that negative pressure is maintained if:

item.p: a production building has only one working space and this emits an annual load at least 500 kg of VOCs;
a production building has several working spaces and they emit an annual total load of at least 1000 kg of VOCs; or
a production building has several working spaces and one of these working spaces emits an annual load of at least 500 kg of VOCs.

content.p: Containers for VOCs must be fitted with suitable caps.
1 Up-to-date working regulations must be provided regulating the low-emission handling of solvents. Regulations must also be provided on how to deal with leakages of solvents.
2 Employees must be trained regularly in how to apply the working regulations.
3 Compliance with working regulations must be verified regularly.

1 An up-to-date inventory of the sources of diffuse VOC emissions and the intake and exhaust air flows must be provided. This contains in particular a quantitative estimate of the emissions from each source.
2 Diffuse VOC emissions must be justified.

item.p: If technically and operationally possible and economically acceptable: vapour recovery system
Otherwise: exhaust air by means of suction hoods or shape-adapted source extractions with appropriate suction capacity via APP
In the case of closed mixing installations: solvent supply via closed system

In other mixing processes: equip container with border sealed cover; exhaust air from penetrations by means of suction hoods or shape-adapted source extractions with appropriate extraction capacity via APP
Drying and stoving when printing, laminating and coating
Cleaning of containers, products and componentsa and general cleaning
Cleaning if technically possible with water or VOC-free detergents. If VOCs are used, the following requirements apply:
If cleaning is carried out several times a week, cleaning may only take place in closed systems with (external) preparation of the waste solvents

Opening of the cleaning system to remove the cleaned container, products and components must be synchronised with the starting extraction via the ALURA so that no VOC emissions escape into the working space or into the environment
Open manual cleaning and drying only in closed spaces with exhaust air via APP; forced closure of the cover of the cleaning tank immediately after cleaning
Store cleaning utensils contaminated with solvents in sealed containers
In sealed containers or in the closed system; pressure balance with exhaust air via APP or back-pressure valve
Pipeline to waste disposal centre or by means of closed containers
When using halogenated VOCs, Annex 2 No 87 OAPC must be complied with.

content.p: The requirements in terms of this Annex may on request be replaced by other requirements provided diffuse VOC emissions are thereby reduced at least to the same extent.
1 The FOEN shall issue industry-specific guidelines in order to specify the requirements in terms of this Annex. These may lay down additional industry-specific requirements.
2 It shall review the guidelines in line with technical developments.
3 When issuing or reviewing the guidelines, it shall consult the industries and cantons concerned beforehand.
